_note: Open-items ledger. Papers confirmed MISSED by the tracker and then keyword-fixed, but not yet published in any report. A keyword fix is forward-looking only: it changes what future runs can retrieve, it does NOT carry the specific paper into a report, and the moving harvest window immediately steps past the paper's posting date. This ledger is the carry-forward guarantee. DRAIN IT AT THE START OF EVERY RUN: fetch each status="open" item's metadata, score it with the current scorer, include it if it passes Quality Standards, then set status="resolved" and reported=<YYYY-MM-DD>. If it fails the relevance bar, set status="dropped" with a reason. See prompts/daily-paper-tracker.md -> 'Open-items ledger'.

items.title: Hippocampal Reactivation Trades Episodic Detail for Semantic Gist in Human Memory
items.authors: Hindy, N. C.; Coleman, R.; Selvam, S. R. M. (College of Charleston; VU Amsterdam; U Louisville)
items.note: Confirmed miss. Surfaced by an October 2026 PsyPost/Dispatch Times news cycle, but JOCN issue 38(8) published 2026-04-05 - out of window for every run in September/October. Never previously reported. Squarely on-pillar: high-resolution fMRI in 24 participants shows CA1 reactivation frequency during a 90-s post-encoding delay has OPPOSING relations with later memory - more reactivation predicts MORE false recognition of semantic lures (gist, dz=0.52) but WORSE voice-discrimination/source accuracy (dz=-0.65), a bidirectional CA1 effect of paired dz=1.00, strongest in anterior-to-mid hippocampus. Directly relevant to the Schema-Episodic pillar (schema-driven gist extraction competitively weakening episode-specific detail) and to Encoding-Retrieval. Drain and publish with a [backfill] marker.

items.title: Sleep forms flexible context representations in toddlers
items.authors: Bastian, L.; Kurz, E.-M.; Gutjahr, L.; Noack, H.; ... Born, J. (University of Tuebingen)
items.note: Boundary miss found 2026-10-19: posted 2026-10-12, one day before this run's window opened (10-13) and one day after the previous run's window closed (10-09 -> 10-14). Never reported. On-pillar: toddlers (2-3 y) familiarized with two spatial contexts then nap (~90 min) vs wake; only after sleep did they show significant context memory and stronger toy-context associations; context memory correlated with spindle density and SO-spindle phase-amplitude coupling during NREM. Spatial context is a core episodic component and the spindle/PAC result is the mechanism. Drain and publish with a [backfill] marker.

items.title: Neural subspace reorganization reflects value-based decision-making
items.authors: Li, H.; Chrysanthidis, N.; Brincat, S. L.; Rose, J.; Miller, E. K. (MIT; Radboud)
items.note: Confirmed miss by metadata gap: in window for the 2026-10-19 run, but Crossref returns only month-level dating (2026-10) and an empty abstract, so approach/finding could not be stated under the Quality Standards. LPFC recordings in non-human primates holding two sequentially presented option-value pairs in WM; once a decision could be made, chosen and unchosen representations rotated into orthogonal neural subspaces while the chosen representation expanded; before decision, organization was by presentation order; after, the chosen option moved into a common action-aligned subspace regardless of order. Relevant to Encoding-Retrieval / working-memory geometry. Next run: fetch the abstract from ScienceDirect or PubMed and publish with a [backfill] marker.
